purpose: Phase-4 DRUG RELEASE registry for the Profile-B simulator. Defines ONLY the release of the encapsulated payload from an NLC carrier AFTER it has arrived at the target region: the kinetic model, the release lifecycle states, the trigger, and integrity flags. This is a SEPARATE biological process from transport - transport ends, release begins, they never mix. The code hardcodes NO biology; the kinetic model + provenance live here. NOTHING beyond release is defined (no uptake, membrane crossing, endocytosis, PK, PD, etc.).
authoritative_source: data/profile-b-evidence-package.json (FROZEN). Chen 2012: release kinetics fit to zero-order / first-order / Higuchi / Ritger-Peppas; FIRST-ORDER selected (good correlation). Release time series 1-48 h. The rate constant k is NOT restated in the frozen package and is treated as NOT REPORTED (schematic).

release_model.name: First-order release
release_model.selected_by: chen_2012 - kinetics fit to zero-order, first-order, Higuchi and Ritger-Peppas; FIRST-ORDER selected (good correlation)
release_model.notes: The MODEL choice (first-order) is directly reported. It is a FORMULATION property (in-vitro release of the NLC into receptor medium), not a species property. The numeric rate constant k and the exact % released are NOT restated in the frozen package.

rate_constant.note: The frozen package reports the first-order MODEL and the 1-48 h release window but NOT a numeric k. The simulator therefore uses a SCHEMATIC rate (engine config) anchored to span the reported window; it is NOT a measured constant and no exact %-released value is claimed.

states.name: Loaded
states.description: Carrier holds its full payload; release has not begun (particle has not yet arrived, or has just arrived).

states.name: Releasing
states.description: Payload is leaving the carrier following first-order kinetics; drug inside decreases, released amount increases.

states.name: Empty
states.description: Payload has been released (asymptotic depletion reached the empty threshold).

trigger.note: Release begins ONLY after transport ends. The release engine reads (never writes) the transport status; it never moves particles. Transport and release are separate processes and never mix.

payload.crystallinity_note: Chen 2012: tripterine is AMORPHOUS in the surface-charged NLCs (supports simple diffusion-limited release; no crystallisation complication modelled).
payload.charge_note: Chen reports the release ORDER differs with surface charge, but the frozen package does not restate per-charge numbers - so charge is a LABEL only and a single schematic first-order rate is used (no per-charge k fabricated).
payload.conservation: released_fraction + payload_fraction = 1 at all times (mass conservation within the release domain).

integrity.separation: Drug release is a COMPLETELY separate process from transport. The transport engine only moves particles; the release engine only releases payload from ARRIVED particles. Neither modifies the other's state.
integrity.schematic_rate: The first-order MODEL is evidence-based (reported). The rate magnitude k is NOT REPORTED -> schematic, anchored to the reported 1-48 h window; no quantitative %-released, k, or timing claim is made.
integrity.formulation_level: Release kinetics are a FORMULATION property (same NLC regardless of the skin it was applied to); the model is NOT species-specific and NO per-species k is fabricated. For predictive-transport species (human/mouse, Phase 3.1) the ARRIVAL remains predictive; the release MODEL is the formulation's reported first-order kinetics.
integrity.ends_at_empty: This phase ends when the particle becomes empty. Nothing further is modelled.

provenance_sources: data/profile-b-evidence-package.json (FROZEN) - Chen 2012 release kinetics: FIRST-ORDER selected; release time series 1-48 h; tripterine amorphous in NLC
Chen Y et al. Int J Nanomedicine 2012;7:3023-3033 (DOI 10.2147/IJN.S32476) - primary full-text source
